name: Zond 5
short_status: Uncrewed circumlunar flight, Sep 14-21, 1968: first spacecraft (and first Earth life, two steppe tortoises) to loop around the Moon and return safely to Earth.
tagline: Soviet Union · Flyby · 1968 · The space race Success
stats: closest pass over the lunar far side, Sep 18, 1968
first Earth life to travel around the Moon and return
launch to Indian Ocean splashdown, Sep 14-21, 1968
distance of its high-quality Earth photographs

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 14 September 1968, 21:42:11 UTC (00:42 September 15 Moscow time), Proton-K + Blok D, Baikonur (NIIP-5) Site 81/23

facts.label: Spacecraft
facts.value: Soyuz 7K-L1 no. 9L, c. 5,375 kg, built by TsKBEM for the crewed circumlunar program

facts.label: Trans-lunar injection
facts.value: Blok D restart about 67 minutes after launch, from a 191 x 219 km parking orbit

facts.label: Lunar far-side pass
facts.value: 1,950 km closest approach (NASA's figure; NSSDCA and RussianSpaceWeb give 1,960 km), 18 September 1968; free-return trajectory, no lunar orbit

facts.label: Biological payload
facts.value: 2 steppe (Horsfield's) tortoises at 0.34-0.40 kg each, Drosophila eggs, dried wheat/barley/pea/carrot/tomato cells, Tradescantia plant, 3 chlorella strains, lysogenic bacteria

facts.label: Earth photography
facts.value: High-quality photographs of Earth from about 90,000 km, plus far-side lunar imagery

facts.label: Voice incident
facts.value: Night of 19-20 September 1968: Jodrell Bank heard a Russian voice (a comms test, presumed tape-recorded or relayed) calling out instrument values from the spacecraft

facts.label: Reentry
facts.value: Guided-skip reentry system switched off after a second attitude-sensor failure; direct ballistic reentry into the backup recovery zone

facts.label: Splashdown
facts.value: 21 September 1968, 16:08 UTC, Indian Ocean at 32 deg 38 min S, 65 deg 33 min E, 105 km from the nearest Soviet tracking ship; mission duration 6 days 18 hours 24 minutes

facts.label: Recovery
facts.value: Recovered by Soviet ships Borovichy and Vasiliy Golovnin; capsule delivered to Mumbai (Bombay) 3 October 1968 for return to the USSR

facts.label: Tortoise outcome
facts.value: Survived; back in Moscow October 7; dissection October 11 after a 39-day fast attributed the main changes to starvation rather than to spaceflight (about 10% body-weight loss)

facts.label: Legacy
facts.value: First successful circumlunar mission by any nation; with N-1 reconnaissance imagery, it fed NASA's decision to fly Apollo 8 to lunar orbit in December 1968

timeline: Two flight tortoises sealed aboard; feeding stops so spaceflight effects can be isolated
21:42 UTC (15 Sep Moscow time): launch from Baikonur Site 81/23 on Proton-K; Blok D restart sends it moonward about 67 minutes later
03:11 UTC: midcourse correction at 325,000 km using backup Sun/Earth sensors after the 100K star tracker fails from contamination
Loops 1,950 km above the lunar far side on a free-return trajectory; photographs the Moon and Earth
Jodrell Bank hears a Russian voice calling out instrument values from the returning craft, a comms rehearsal that briefly reads as a crewed flight
16:08 UTC: ballistic reentry into the backup zone; splashdown in the Indian Ocean at 32 deg 38 min S, 65 deg 33 min E; first successful circumlunar return
Recovery ship Vasiliy Golovnin delivers the capsule to Mumbai (Bombay) for return to the USSR
Tortoises reach Moscow Oct 7; dissection Oct 11 traces the changes to their 39-day fast instead of to spaceflight
Apollo 8, greenlit partly on fear of a crewed Zond, orbits the Moon with humans aboard
